  scope :expired, -> { where(completed_at: ...DOWNLOAD_EXPIRY.ago) }

      expired.find_each(&:destroy)
    end
  end

    ExportJob.perform_later(self)

    processing!
    write_file

  rescue => error
    failed!
    ExportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
    raise
  end

    completed? && !expired?

  def expired?
    completed_at.present? && completed_at < DOWNLOAD_EXPIRY.ago

# Brings an exported account back in as a brand new account, with the person importing it as a member.
class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :identity
  belongs_to :account, optional: true

  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  validate :file_attached, on: :create

  after_create_commit :process_later

  def process_later
    Account::ImportJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def process_now
    processing!
    update! account: import_account, status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current
    account.reindex_search_later
    Account::ImportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
  rescue => error
    update! status: :failed, failure_reason: failure_reason_for(error), completed_at: Time.current
    Account::ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
    Rails.error.report(error, severity: :error)
  ensure
    file.purge_later
  end

  private
    def file_attached
      errors.add(:file, "must be attached") unless file.attached?
    end

    def import_account
      ZipFile.open(file) do |zip|
        Account::DataTransfer::Importer.new(zip, id_mapper: id_mapper).import do |account|
          identity.join account, role: :owner, verified_at: Time.current
        end
      end
    end

    def id_mapper
      Account::DataTransfer::IdMapper.new(id)
    end

    def failure_reason_for(error)
      case error
      when Account::DataTransfer::Importer::InvalidFile
        error.message
      when ZipKit::FileReader::ReadError, ZipKit::FileReader::MissingEOCD, ZipKit::FileReader::UnsupportedFeature, ZipFile::Reader::MissingEntry, Zlib::Error
        "The file isn't a valid ZIP archive (#{error.message})"
      else
        "Something went wrong while importing (#{error.class.name}: #{error.message})"
      end
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class Account::ExportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
    @user = users(:kevin)
  end

  test "creating an export processes it later" do
    assert_enqueued_with job: ExportJob do
      Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)
    end
  end

  test "processing packs the whole account into a zip and emails a download link" do
    cards(:logo).image.attach(io: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open, filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg")
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)

    assert_enqueued_emails 1 do
      export.process_now
    end

    assert export.completed?
    assert export.downloadable?
    assert export.file.attached?
    assert_equal "application/zip", export.file.content_type
    assert_match(/\Aexport-37signals-\d+\.zip\z/, export.file.filename.to_s)

    ZipFile.open(export.file) do |zip|
      manifest = JSON.parse(zip.read("manifest.json"))
      assert_equal "fizzy-account-export", manifest["format"]
      assert_equal @account.id, manifest.dig("account", "id")

      assert_equal [ @account.id ], JSON.parse(zip.read("accounts/000000.json")).map { it["id"] }
      assert_equal @account.cards.count, zip.glob("cards/*.json").sum { JSON.parse(zip.read(it)).size }
      assert_equal @account.boards.count, zip.glob("boards/*.json").sum { JSON.parse(zip.read(it)).size }
      assert_equal Comment.where(account: @account).count, zip.glob("comments/*.json").sum { JSON.parse(zip.read(it)).size }

      users = JSON.parse(zip.read("users/000000.json"))
      assert_includes users.map { it["email_address"] }, "kevin@37signals.com"
      assert_equal @account.users.count, users.size

      blob = cards(:logo).image.blob
      assert zip.exists?("files/#{blob.key}")
      assert_equal file_fixture("moon.jpg").binread, zip.read("files/#{blob.key}")
    end
  end

  test "the export's own file is not part of the exported data" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)
    export.process_now

    ZipFile.open(export.file) do |zip|
      blobs = zip.glob("active_storage_blobs/*.json").flat_map { JSON.parse(zip.read(it)) }
      assert_not_includes blobs.map { it["id"] }, export.file.blob.id
    end
  end

  test "a failed export is marked as such and emails the requester" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)
    Account::DataTransfer::Exporter.any_instance.stubs(:export_to).raises("boom")

    assert_enqueued_emails 1 do
      assert_raises(RuntimeError) { export.process_now }
    end

    assert export.failed?
    assert_not export.downloadable?
  end

  test "download links expire after a day" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)
    export.process_now

    assert export.downloadable?
    assert_not export.expired?

    travel Export::DOWNLOAD_EXPIRY + 1.minute do
      assert export.expired?
      assert_not export.downloadable?
    end
  end

  test "cleanup destroys expired exports along with their files" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)
    export.process_now
    fresh_export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)

    travel Export::DOWNLOAD_EXPIRY + 1.minute do
      assert_difference -> { Export.count }, -1 do
        Export.cleanup
      end
    end

    assert_not Export.exists?(export.id)
    assert Export.exists?(fresh_export.id)
  end

  test "account exports can be downloaded by the requester and by other admins" do
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)

    assert export.accessible_to?(@user)
    assert export.accessible_to?(users(:jason))
    assert_not export.accessible_to?(users(:david))
    assert_not export.accessible_to?(users(:mike))
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class User::ExportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @user = users(:david)
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
  end

  test "packs the cards a user can see as JSON with comments and attached files" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    card.image.attach(io: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open, filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg")
    embed = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: file_fixture("avatar.png").open, filename: "avatar.png", content_type: "image/png")
    comment = card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "See attached #{ActionText::Attachment.from_attachable(embed).to_html}")

    export = User::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)

    assert_enqueued_emails 1 do
      export.process_now
    end

    assert export.completed?

    ZipFile.open(export.file) do |zip|
      assert_equal @user.accessible_cards.published.count, zip.glob("cards/*/card.json").size

      json = JSON.parse(zip.read("cards/#{card.number}/card.json"))
      assert_equal card.title, json["title"]
      assert_equal card.board.name, json.dig("board", "name")
      assert_includes json["comments"].map { it["id"] }, comment.id
      assert_equal "See attached", json["comments"].find { it["id"] == comment.id }["body"].strip

      assert_equal [ "cards/#{card.number}/files/moon.jpg" ], json["files"].map { it["path"] }
      assert_equal file_fixture("moon.jpg").binread, zip.read("cards/#{card.number}/files/moon.jpg")

      comment_files = json["comments"].find { it["id"] == comment.id }["files"]
      assert_equal [ "cards/#{card.number}/files/avatar.png" ], comment_files.map { it["path"] }
      assert_equal file_fixture("avatar.png").binread, zip.read("cards/#{card.number}/files/avatar.png")

      assert zip.exists?("cards/#{cards(:logo).number}/card.json")
    end
  end

  test "only the user can download their export" do
    export = User::Export.create!(account: @account, user: @user)

    assert_not export.accessible_to?(users(:jason))

end

arguments.command:
cd /app; cat <<'EOF' > test/models/account/import_test.rb
require "test_helper"

class Account::ImportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionMailer::TestHelper

  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
    @identity = Identity.create!(email_address: "newcomer@example.com")
  end

  test "creating an import processes it later" do
    assert_enqueued_with job: Account::ImportJob do
      import_for exported_account_file
    end
  end

  test "importing an export creates a new account with everything in it" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    card.image.attach(io: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open, filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg")
    embed = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: file_fixture("avatar.png").open, filename: "avatar.png", content_type: "image/png")
    comment = card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Hey #{ActionText::Attachment.from_attachable(users(:jz)).to_html} look at #{ActionText::Attachment.from_attachable(embed).to_html}")
    card.assignments.create!(assignee: users(:jz))

    import = import_for(exported_account_file)

    assert_enqueued_emails 1 do
      assert_difference -> { Account.count }, +1 do
        Current.without_account { import.process_now }
      end
    end

    assert import.completed?, import.failure_reason
    account = import.account
    assert_not_equal @account, account
    assert_not_equal @account.external_account_id, account.external_account_id
    assert_equal @account.name, account.name
    assert_equal @account.created_at.to_i, account.created_at.to_i
    assert account.join_code.present?

    assert_equal @account.boards.count, account.boards.count
    assert_equal @account.boards.pluck(:name).sort, account.boards.pluck(:name).sort
    assert_equal @account.cards.count, account.cards.count
    assert_equal @account.columns.count, account.columns.count
    assert_equal @account.tags.count, account.tags.count
    assert_equal Comment.where(account: @account).count, Comment.where(account: account).count
    assert_equal Event.where(account: @account).count, Event.where(account: account).count
    assert_equal Access.where(account: @account).count, Access.where(account: account).count
    assert_equal @account.entropy.auto_postpone_period, account.entropy.auto_postpone_period
    assert_equal 1, account.entropies.where(container: account).count

    imported_card = account.cards.find_by!(number: card.number)
    assert_equal card.title, imported_card.title
    assert_equal card.board.name, imported_card.board.name
    assert_equal card.created_at.to_i, imported_card.created_at.to_i
    assert_equal card.creator.identity.email_address, imported_card.creator.identity.email_address
    assert_equal [ "jz@37signals.com" ], imported_card.assignees.map { it.identity.email_address }

    assert imported_card.image.attached?
    assert_not_equal card.image.blob.id, imported_card.image.blob.id
    assert_not_equal card.image.blob.key, imported_card.image.blob.key
    assert_equal card.image.blob.checksum, imported_card.image.blob.checksum
    assert_equal file_fixture("moon.jpg").binread, imported_card.image.download

    imported_comment = imported_card.comments.sole
    assert_equal "kevin@37signals.com", imported_comment.creator.identity.email_address
    mention, attachment = imported_comment.body.body.attachables
    assert_equal account.users.find_by!(name: "JZ"), mention
    assert_kind_of ActiveStorage::Blob, attachment
    assert_equal account, attachment.account
    assert_equal file_fixture("avatar.png").binread, attachment.download
    assert_equal imported_comment.attachments.map(&:blob), [ attachment ]
  end

  test "people are linked to their identities by email address and the importer joins as owner" do
    import = import_for(exported_account_file)
    Current.without_account { import.process_now }
    account = import.account

    assert_equal @account.users.count + 1, account.users.count
    assert_equal users(:kevin).identity, account.users.find_by!(name: "Kevin").identity
    assert_equal users(:kevin).role, account.users.find_by!(name: "Kevin").role
    assert account.users.find_by!(name: "System").system?

    newcomer = account.users.find_by!(identity: @identity)
    assert newcomer.owner?
    assert newcomer.verified?
    assert_equal account.boards.all_access.count, newcomer.boards.count
  end

  test "an importer who was already in the account keeps their user" do
    import = import_for(exported_account_file, identity: users(:david).identity)
    Current.without_account { import.process_now }

    assert import.completed?, import.failure_reason
    assert_equal @account.users.count, import.account.users.count
    assert import.account.users.find_by!(identity: users(:david).identity).member?
  end

  test "importing the same export twice creates two separate accounts" do
    file = exported_account_file

    first = import_for(file)
    Current.without_account { first.process_now }
    second = import_for(file)
    Current.without_account { second.process_now }

    assert first.completed?, first.failure_reason
    assert second.completed?, second.failure_reason
    assert_not_equal first.account, second.account
    assert_equal @account.cards.count, second.account.cards.count
  end

  test "a file that isn't a Fizzy export fails and leaves nothing behind" do
    import = import_for(zip_file_with("readme.txt" => "Hello"))

    assert_enqueued_emails 1 do
      assert_no_difference -> { Account.count } do
        Current.without_account { import.process_now }
      end
    end

    assert import.failed?
    assert_nil import.account
    assert_match(/doesn't look like a Fizzy account export/, import.failure_reason)
  end

  test "a file that isn't a zip fails gracefully" do
    import = import_for(Tempfile.new.tap { it.write("not a zip"); it.rewind })

    assert_no_difference -> { Account.count } do
      Current.without_account { import.process_now }
    end

    assert import.failed?
    assert_match(/isn't a valid ZIP archive/, import.failure_reason)
  end

  test "an import that fails midway rolls everything back, including uploaded files" do
    cards(:logo).image.attach(io: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open, filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg")
    import = import_for(exported_account_file)
    Account::DataTransfer::ActionText::RichTextRecordSet.any_instance.stubs(:import_from).raises("boom")

    uploaded_keys = []
    ActiveStorage::Blob.service.stubs(:upload).with { |key, *| uploaded_keys << key }

    assert_no_difference -> { [ Account.count, User.count, Card.count, ActiveStorage::Blob.count, Identity.count ] } do
      Current.without_account { import.process_now }
    end

    assert import.failed?
    assert_match(/boom/, import.failure_reason)
    assert uploaded_keys.any?
    uploaded_keys.each { |key| assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(key) }
  end

  test "the uploaded file is purged once the import is over" do
    import = import_for(exported_account_file)

    Current.without_account do
      perform_enqueued_jobs(only: ActiveStorage::PurgeJob) { import.process_now }
    end

    assert_not import.reload.file.attached?
  end

  private
    def exported_account_file
      export = Account::Export.create!(account: @account, user: users(:kevin))
      export.process_now
      Tempfile.new([ "export", ".zip" ]).tap do |file|
        file.binmode
        file.write(export.file.download)
        file.rewind
      end
    end

    def zip_file_with(files)
      Tempfile.new([ "bogus", ".zip" ]).tap do |file|
        file.binmode
        writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(file)
        files.each { |path, content| writer.add_file(path, content) }
        writer.close
        file.rewind
      end
    end

    def import_for(file, identity: @identity)
      Current.without_account do
        identity.imports.create!(file: { io: file, filename: "export.zip", content_type: "application/zip" })
      end
    end
end
EOF

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm setting up the assignment creation with jz and kevin as assignee and assigner. For the rollback test, I'm considering stubbing the blob service's upload method so files never actually get written, letting me verify existence checks and upload tracking stay false—though I need to think through whether this stubbing approach is actually the right way to test the rollback behavior.

Actually, I decide a cleaner approach is comparing the disk service's file count before and after a failed import, since stubbing upload prevents verifying the delete cleanup happens correctly. I'm sketching a test that globs files in the service root directory, captures the count before an import failure, then asserts the count matches afterward to confirm no orphaned blobs remain.

To make sure files actually get uploaded before the rollback occurs, I move the failure trigger to happen after the FileRecordSet finishes—raising an error during the identity join step instead of earlier in the record set processing, so the transaction rollback happens post-upload rather than trivially skipping it. I'm also thinking through how the purge job gets enqueued and tested with `perform_enqueued_jobs`.

# Rich text embeds files and mentions people through signed global IDs, which are only valid
# on the instance that signed them and point at the original records. They travel as plain
# global IDs and get remapped and signed again on the way in.
class Account::DataTransfer::ActionText::RichTextRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  ATTACHMENT_SELECTOR = ::ActionText::Attachment.tag_name
  PORTABLE_ID_ATTRIBUTE = "gid"

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActionText::RichText)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActionText::RichText.where(account: account)
    end

    # Bodies are read raw: deserializing them would look up every attachment in the database
    def serialize_attribute(record, name)
      if name == "body"
        portable_body record.read_attribute_before_type_cast("body")
      else
        super
      end
    end

    def portable_body(html)
      rewrite_attachments_in(html, "#{ATTACHMENT_SELECTOR}[sgid]") do |node|
        if sgid = SignedGlobalID.parse(node["sgid"], for: ::ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME)
          node[PORTABLE_ID_ATTRIBUTE] = global_id_for(sgid.model_name, sgid.model_id)
        end

        node.remove_attribute("sgid")
      end
    end

    def deserialize(row, id_mapper)
      super.tap do |attributes|
        attributes["body"] = local_body(attributes["body"], id_mapper) if attributes.key?("body")
      end
    end

    def local_body(html, id_mapper)
      rewrite_attachments_in(html, "#{ATTACHMENT_SELECTOR}[#{PORTABLE_ID_ATTRIBUTE}]") do |node|
        if gid = GlobalID.parse(node[PORTABLE_ID_ATTRIBUTE])
          node["sgid"] = signed_global_id_for(gid.model_name, id_mapper.map(gid.model_id))
        end

        node.remove_attribute(PORTABLE_ID_ATTRIBUTE)
      end
    end

    def global_id_for(model_name, id)
      URI::GID.build(app: GlobalID.app, model_name: model_name, model_id: id).to_s
    end

    def signed_global_id_for(model_name, id)
      SignedGlobalID.new(global_id_for(model_name, id), for: ::ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME, expires_in: nil).to_s
    end

    def rewrite_attachments_in(html, selector)
      if html.present?
        fragment = ::ActionText::Fragment.wrap(html)
        nodes = fragment.find_all(selector)

        if nodes.any?
          nodes.each { |node| yield node }
          fragment.to_html
        else
          html
        end
      else
        html
      end
    end
end

I realize filters also embed card and column UUIDs inside their fields JSON, so those need remapping too, along with recomputing the params_digest afterward — but since that digest depends on association ids that only exist after join tables are imported, I'll need to handle digest recalculation as a later post-processing step.

Since join rows live in separate files, the cleanest approach is probably to recompute all filter digests after the entire import finishes, iterating over filters and recalculating `params_digest` from their loaded associations. Alternatively, I could reorder the import manifest so join tables get processed before filters, avoiding the need for a separate finalize pass.

Reordering seems simplest since join rows conceptually depend on filters, so I'll put resource sets before FilterRecordSet with a comment explaining why, and recompute digests there since the needed tag/board/assignee ids aren't available otherwise. Actually, I'm second-guessing whether a stale digest even matters, since `before_save` recomputes it and `Filter.remember` falls back to `find_by_params` on a uniqueness violation anyway.

# Filters keep IDs of cards and columns in their fields, and a digest of all their params
# that has to be worked out again once every ID they point at has been remapped.
class Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  REMAPPED_FIELDS = %w[ card_ids column_ids ]

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: Filter)
  end

  private
    def deserialize(row, id_mapper)
      super.tap do |attributes|
        if fields = attributes["fields"]
          REMAPPED_FIELDS.each do |name|
            fields[name] = fields[name].map { |id| id_mapper.map(id) } if fields[name].is_a?(Array)
          end
        end
      end
    end

    # Digests cover the tags, boards and people a filter refers to, so they can only be worked
    # out once those join rows are in: filter resources are imported right before filters.
    def import_rows(rows)
      super

      Filter.where(id: rows.map { |row| row["id"] }).find_each do |filter|
        filter.update_columns params_digest: Filter.digest_params(filter.as_params)
      end
    end
end
EOF

class Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES = %w[ Export Account::Import ].freeze
  BATCH_SIZE = 500

  def initialize(account:, model:, attributes: nil)

    @model = model
    @attributes = (attributes || model.column_names).map(&:to_s)
  end

        write_rows batch.map { |record| serialize(record) }, index: index
      end
    end
  end

    with_zip(zip) do
      each_exported_rows do |rows|

  end

      @zip = zip
      yield

    end

      model.table_name

    end

    def serialize(record)
      attributes.index_with { |name| serialize_attribute(record, name) }
    end

    def serialize_attribute(record, name)
      serialize_value record.read_attribute(name)
    end

    def serialize_value(value)
      case value
      when Time
        value.utc.iso8601(6)
      else
        value
      end
    end

    def each_exported_rows
      zip.glob("#{model_dir}/*.json").each do |path|
        rows = JSON.parse(zip.read(path))
        yield rows if rows.any?
      end
    end

    # Only known columns are imported, so exports from other versions of Fizzy still load.
    def deserialize(row, id_mapper)
      row.slice(*attributes).tap do |attributes|
        uuid_attributes.each do |name|
          attributes[name] = id_mapper.map(attributes[name]) if attributes.key?(name)
        end
      end

    def uuid_attributes
      @uuid_attributes ||= attributes.select { |name| model.columns_hash[name]&.type == :uuid }
    end

    def import_rows(rows)

  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Creates a brand new account out of an export. Everything happens in a single transaction and
# uploaded files are discarded on failure, so an import that can't be completed leaves nothing behind.
class Account::DataTransfer::Importer
  class InvalidFile < StandardError; end

  attr_reader :zip, :id_mapper

  def initialize(zip, id_mapper:)
    @zip = zip
    @id_mapper = id_mapper
  end

  def import
    header = read_manifest_header

    Account.transaction do
      manifest.each_record_set { |record_set| record_set.import_from(zip, id_mapper) }

      Account.find(id_mapper.map(header.dig("account", "id"))).tap do |account|
        yield account if block_given?
      end
    end
  rescue
    manifest.each_record_set(&:rollback_import)
    raise
  end

  private
    def read_manifest_header
      unless zip.exists?(Account::DataTransfer::MANIFEST_FILENAME)
        raise InvalidFile, "The file doesn't look like a Fizzy account export"
      end

      JSON.parse(zip.read(Account::DataTransfer::MANIFEST_FILENAME)).tap do |header|
        unless header["format"] == Account::DataTransfer::FORMAT && header.dig("account", "id").present?
          raise InvalidFile, "The file doesn't look like a Fizzy account export"
        end

        if header["version"].to_i > Account::DataTransfer::VERSION
          raise InvalidFile, "The file was exported by a newer version of Fizzy and can't be imported here"
        end
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise InvalidFile, "The file doesn't look like a Fizzy account export"
    end

    # Imports have no account until the account record set creates one
    def manifest
      @manifest ||= Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(nil)
    end
end
# The contents of every blob, stored uncompressed under files/ so they can be streamed straight
# in and out of the storage service.
class Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActiveStorage::Blob)
    @uploaded_blobs = []
  end

  def export_to(zip)
    with_zip(zip) do
      records.find_each do |blob|
        zip.add_file(path_for(blob.key), compress: false) do |sink|
          blob.download { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def import_from(zip, id_mapper)
    with_zip(zip) do
      each_exported_rows do |rows|
        rows.each { |row| upload(row, id_mapper) }
      end
    end
  end

  def rollback_import
    @uploaded_blobs.each do |blob|
      blob.service.delete(blob.key)
    end
    @uploaded_blobs.clear
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account: account).where.not(id: excluded_blob_ids)
    end

    def excluded_blob_ids
      ::ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account: account, record_type: INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES).select(:blob_id)
    end

    def path_for(key)
      "files/#{key}"
    end

    def upload(row, id_mapper)
      blob = ::ActiveStorage::Blob.find(id_mapper.map(row["id"]))

      Tempfile.create("import", binmode: true) do |tempfile|
        zip.extract(path_for(row["key"]), to: tempfile)
        tempfile.rewind

        @uploaded_blobs << blob
        blob.upload_without_unfurling(tempfile)
      end
    end
end
# Reads entries out of a ZIP archive through an IO-ish object (#read, #seek, #tell, #size),
# so that huge archives can be read from local disk or from remote storage without ever
# loading the whole file into memory.
class ZipFile::Reader
  CHUNK_SIZE = 8.megabytes

  class MissingEntry < StandardError; end

  def initialize(io)
    @io = io
    @file_reader = ZipKit::FileReader.new
    @entries = @file_reader.read_zip_structure(io: io, read_local_headers: false).index_by(&:filename)
  end

  def entries
    @entries.keys
  end

  def glob(pattern)
    entries.select { |path| File.fnmatch(pattern, path) }.sort
  end

  def exists?(path)
    @entries.key?(path)
  end

  def size_of(path)
    entry_for(path).uncompressed_size
  end

  def read(path)
    StringIO.new.binmode.tap { |io| extract(path, to: io) }.string
  end

  # Streams the uncompressed contents of an entry into anything that responds to #write.
  def extract(path, to:)
    extractor = extractor_for(entry_for(path))

    until extractor.eof?
      chunk = extractor.extract(CHUNK_SIZE)
      break if chunk.nil?
      to.write(chunk)
    end
  end

  private
    def entry_for(path)
      @entries.fetch(path) { raise MissingEntry, "No entry named #{path} in ZIP file" }
    end

    def extractor_for(entry)
      unless entry.known_offset?
        entry.compressed_data_offset = @file_reader.get_compressed_data_offset(io: @io, local_file_header_offset: entry.local_file_header_offset)
      end

      entry.extractor_from(@io)
    end
end
"

If you want to run your own Fizzy instance, but don't need to change its code, you can use our pre-built Docker image.
You'll need access to a server on which you can run Docker, and you'll need to configure some options to customize your installation.

You can find the details of how to do a Docker-based deployment in our [Docker deployment guide](docs/docker-deployment.md).

If you want more flexibility to customize your Fizzy installation by changing its code, and deploy those changes to your server, then we recommend you deploy Fizzy with Kamal. You can find a complete walkthrough of doing that in our [Kamal deployment guide](docs/kamal-deployment.md).


## Development

You are welcome -- and encouraged -- to modify Fizzy to your liking.
Please see our [Development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Fizzy set up for local development.


## Contributing

We welcome contributions! Please read our [style guide](STYLE.md) before submitting code.

steps.message:
Everything is green: full suite (1500 tests), rubocop (only a pre-existing offense in `routes.rb`), and brakeman. Here's a summary of what I built.

## Summary

**Exports** (`Export` STI base → `Account::Export`, `User::Export`)
- **Account export** — an admin clicks "Export account…" in account settings (`POST /account/exports`). `ExportJob` streams the whole account into one ZIP via `ZipFile.create_for` (disk or S3, existing code): a `manifest.json` header, every table's rows as batched JSON (`cards/000000.json`, `comments/…`, …), and every blob's bytes under `files/<key>`.
- **Cards export** — anyone clicks "Download my cards…" on their own profile (`POST /my/exports`). `User::Export::CardWriter` writes `cards/<number>/card.json` (card + comments + reactions + steps) plus every picture/file attached to the card or its comments under `cards/<number>/files/`.
- `ExportMailer.ready` emails a link (`GET /account/exports/:id`, `/my/exports/:id`) that redirects to the file; links stop working after `Export::DOWNLOAD_EXPIRY` (1 day), and a recurring `Export.cleanup` purges expired files. Only one export runs at a time per account/user, and blob downloads are authorized through `Export#accessible_to?`.

**Imports** (`Account::Import`, identity-level at `/account/imports/new`)
- Anyone signed in uploads an export; `Account::ImportJob` → `Account::DataTransfer::Importer` recreates the account inside **one transaction**, and `rollback_import` deletes any files already uploaded on failure — so a failed import leaves nothing behind. `Account::ImportMailer` sends "done" (link to the new account) or "failed" with the reason, and the uploaded file is purged either way.
- Every record gets a **fresh ID** via `IdMapper` (deterministic per import, preserving UUIDv7 ordering), so an export can be re-imported anywhere, even into the same instance. People are re-linked by email (`Identity.find_or_create_by!`), and the importer joins as owner if they weren't already a member.
- Rich text mentions/embeds travel as portable `gid`s (`RichTextRecordSet`) and are re-signed for the remapped records; `Event` particulars, `Filter` fields/digests and their join tables, blob keys, and the account's default entropy are all handled. Search index and storage totals are rebuilt afterwards by jobs.

**Infrastructure**
- `ZipFile::Reader` + `ZipFile::RemoteIO` read huge ZIPs without downloading them (ranged reads through the storage service with buffering).
- Migrations for `exports`/`account_imports`; blob/attachment `account_id` made nullable so an import file can exist before its account does (mirrored in both `schema.rb` and `schema_sqlite.rb`).
